question:
Arrange the names of the following defence ministers of India from the earliest to latest.
A. Sharad Pawar
B. Mulayam Singh Yadav
C. George Fernandes
D. Rajnath Singh (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: B,D,A,C
C,B,D,A
A,D,C,B
A,B,C,D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A,B,C,D

Explanation:
Sharad Pawar served as Defence Minister from 1988-1989 and again from 1991-1993. Mulayam Singh Yadav held the office from 1996-1998. George Fernandes served three terms: 1998-2001, 2001-2002, and 2003-2004. Rajnath Singh has been Defence Minister from 2014-2019 and then from 2019 onwards (till 2024). Thus, chronological order: Sharad Pawar (earliest), followed by Mulayam Singh Yadav, then George Fernandes, and lastly Rajnath Singh (latest).

☛ Mulayam Singh Yadav's tenure as Defence Minister → 1996-1998
☛ George Fernandes' tenure as Defence Minister → 1998-2002 (three terms)
☛ Rajnath Singh's tenure as Defence Minister → 2014-2019 and 2019-present
☛ Longest serving Defence Minister → Rajnath Singh

question: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, which recognised 'cooperative societies' as a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy, amended which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Articles 39 and 243
Articles 21 and 243
Articles 19 and 39
Articles 19 and 243
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Articles 19 and 243

Explanation:
The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 gave constitutional status to cooperative societies. It amended Article 19(1)(c) to include the right to form cooperative societies as a fundamental right. It also added Articles 243-ZI to 243-ZT, forming Part IX-B, which deals with cooperative societies. Additionally, it inserted Article 43-B into the Directive Principles of State Policy, promoting the voluntary formation of cooperative societies. Articles 39 and 243 were not amended by this Act; Article 243 pertains to Panchayats. Thus, only Articles 19 and 243 were amended, but Article 243 here refers to new provisions under Part IX-B.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the 97th Amendment passed? → 2011
☛ Which Article grants the right to form cooperatives as a fundamental right? → Article 19(1)(c)
☛ Which DPSP relates to cooperative societies? → Article 43-B
☛ Minimum number of members for a cooperative society? → 10
☛ Does the 97th Amendment relate to Part IX-B? → Yes
question_hi: 97वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, जिसने 'सहकारी समितियों' को राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों के भाग के रूप में मान्यता दी, ने भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुच्छेद में संशोधन किया? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 39 और 243
अनुच्छेद 21 और 243
अनुच्छेद 19 और 39
अनुच्छेद 19 और 243
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 19 और 243

Explanation:
97वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2011 ने सहकारी समितियों को संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया। इसने अनुच्छेद 19(1)(c) में संशोधन करके सहकारी समितियाँ बनाने के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकार बनाया। साथ ही, अनुच्छेद 243-ZI से 243-ZT तक जोड़कर सहकारी समितियों से संबंधित प्रावधान शामिल किए। इस अधिनियम ने अनुच्छेद 43-B जोड़ा, जो सहकारी समितियों को राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों में शामिल करता है। अनुच्छेद 39 और 243 में संशोधन नहीं किया गया। अनुच्छेद 243 पंचायती राज से संबंधित है। अतः केवल अनुच्छेद 19 और 243 में संशोधन हुआ।

question: In 1919, when the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were introduced in India, Lord Chelmsford was the: (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Governor General of India
British Prime Minister
Secretary of State for India
Viceroy of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Viceroy of India

Explanation:
When the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (officially the Government of India Act 1919) were introduced in India in 1919, Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy of India. He served in this position from 1916 to 1921. These reforms are known for introducing the dyarchy system in provinces, dividing subjects into reserved and transferred categories. The Secretary of State for India at that time was Edwin Montagu, who collaborated with Lord Chelmsford to prepare the reform report, known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Report, in 1918.

☛ Dyarchy → Division of executive departments in provinces
☛ Edwin Montagu → Secretary of State for India (1917-1922)
☛ Lord Chelmsford → Viceroy of India (1916-1921)
☛ Montagu-Chelmsford Report → Published in 1918

question: What is the minimum age prescribed in the Constitution of India for a person to be appointed as a High Court Judge? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 25 years
No minimum age is prescribed in the Constitution.
32 years
30 years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is No minimum age is prescribed in the Constitution.

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution under Article 217 specifies the qualifications for appointment as a High Court judge, but it does not prescribe any minimum age. In contrast, the Supreme Court judge must be below 65 years of age as per Article 124. For High Court judges, the conditions include: being a citizen of India, having held a judicial office for at least ten years, or having been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years. Since no age limit is mentioned, a qualified person can be appointed at any age. This makes the correct answer that no minimum age is prescribed.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article deals with High Court judge appointment? → Article 217
☛ What is the maximum age for a Supreme Court judge? → 65 years
☛ How many years of advocacy required for High Court judge? → Ten years
☛ Who appoints High Court judges? → President
☛ Is there a minimum age for High Court judge? → No

question: Who appoints the Governor of a state in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Prime Minister
Election Commission
Chief Minister
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
According to Article 155 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor of a state is appointed by the President of India. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and represents the central government. The President appoints the Governor at his own discretion, but in practice, the appointment is made on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers. The Governor holds office for a term of five years, but can be removed earlier by the President. The Governor can only be removed by the President. This process is a crucial part of India's federal system, ensuring coordination between the center and states.

☛ Who can remove the Governor? → President

question_hi: भारत में किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति कौन करता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: प्रधानमंत्री
चुनाव आयोग
मुख्यमंत्री
राष्ट्रपति
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 155 के अनुसार, किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। राज्यपाल राज्य का संवैधानिक प्रमुख होता है और केंद्र सरकार का प्रतिनिधि होता है। राष्ट्रपति राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति अपनी मर्जी से करता है, लेकिन व्यवहार में केंद्रीय मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह से नियुक्ति होती है। राज्यपाल का कार्यकाल प्रायः पांच वर्ष का होता है, लेकिन वह राष्ट्रपति के प्रसादपर्यंत पद पर बना रहता है। राज्यपाल को राष्ट्रपति द्वारा ही हटाया जा सकता है। यह प्रक्रिया भारत की संघीय व्यवस्था का महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है, जो केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच समन्वय सुनिश्चित करती है।

question: Who appoints the Chairman and members of a Joint Administrative Tribunal (JAT)? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The concerned state governments
The Chief Justice of India, in consultation with the Chief Ministers of the concerned states
The President of India, after consultation with the Governors of the concerned states
The Union Cabinet
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India, after consultation with the Governors of the concerned states

Explanation:
A Joint Administrative Tribunal (JAT) is established for two or more states. The Chairman and members of a JAT are appointed by the President of India after consultation with the Governors of the concerned states. This provision is made under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985. The President's decision is final in the appointment process. This system ensures coordination between the Centre and the states. The purpose of a JAT is to provide speedy disposal of disputes related to public service. The President acts as the constitutional head in this process.

☛ What type of disputes does a JAT adjudicate? → Disputes related to public service

संयुक्त प्रशासनिक अधिकरण (JAT) की स्थापना दो या दो से अधिक राज्यों के लिए की जाती है। इसके अध्यक्ष और सदस्यों की नियुक्ति भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा संबंधित राज्यों के राज्यपालों के परामर्श से की जाती है। यह प्रावधान प्रशासनिक अधिकरण अधिनियम, 1985 के तहत किया गया है। नियुक्ति प्रक्रिया में राष्ट्रपति का निर्णय अंतिम होता है। यह प्रणाली केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच समन्वय सुनिश्चित करती है। JAT का उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक सेवा से संबंधित विवादों का त्वरित निपटारा करना है। राष्ट्रपति की भूमिका यहाँ संवैधानिक प्रमुख के रूप में होती है।

question: Which commission was appointed to study the reforms of the Government of India Act, 1919, and suggest further measures for constitutional reforms? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)

Simon Commission

solution:

Explanation:
The British government appointed the Simon Commission in 1928 to study the implementation of the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) and suggest further constitutional reforms. The commission was headed by Sir John Simon and consisted of seven British members. Due to the absence of any Indian member, it was boycotted by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League. The commission submitted its report in 1930, recommending the abolition of diarchy and the introduction of provincial autonomy. This report formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935. question: Protection of life and personal liberty is contained under which Article of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 21

Article 23

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
Article 21 of the Indian Constitution provides for the protection of life and personal liberty. It states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This article is part of Part III (Fundamental Rights). The Supreme Court has given it a wide interpretation, including the right to privacy, right to live with dignity, and right to a clean environment under its ambit. Article 21 protects individuals against the state and cannot be suspended even during a national emergency except when public order is threatened. It is one of the most vital fundamental rights ensuring a life of dignity and freedom.

question: How many Fundamental Duties were mentioned at the time of Constitution enforcement in 1950? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 8
11
0
10
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 0

Explanation:
At the time of enforcement of the Indian Constitution in 1950, there were no Fundamental Duties mentioned. Fundamental Duties were later added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976, which introduced Article 51A containing 10 duties. Subsequently, the 86th Amendment (2002) added one more duty (providing educational opportunities to children aged 6-14), making the total count 11. The original Constitution only contained Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35) and Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51). The recommendation to include duties came from the Swaran Singh Committee. Thus, the number of Fundamental Duties in 1950 was zero.

question: The Indian Councils Act, 1861, initiated the process of decentralisation by restoring legislative powers to which provinces? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Bombay and Madras
United Provinces and Assam
Bihar and Orissa
Punjab and Bengal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bombay and Madras

Explanation:
The Indian Councils Act, 1861 initiated the process of decentralisation in British India. This act restored legislative powers to the provinces of Bombay and Madras, which had been abolished by the Charter Act of 1833. Under this act, a legislative council was established for each province, consisting of the governor and a few members. The act allowed the governor-general to involve provinces in the law-making process, but central control was retained. This step was taken to improve administrative efficiency and address local needs. Later acts in 1892 and 1909 brought further decentralisation. The 1861 Act is considered a landmark in the evolution of India's legislative system.

☛ Charter Act of 1833 → Abolished provincial legislatures
☛ Indian Councils Act, 1892 → Increased member numbers and introduced indirect elections

☛ Decentralisation → Transfer of powers from centre to provinces

question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President of India seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 3)

Article 141
Article 129
Article 148
solution:

Explanation:
Article 143 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court. Under this article, the President can refer any question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its opinion. Article 141 makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts, Article 129 gives the Supreme Court the power to punish for contempt, and Article 148 relates to the Comptroller and Auditor General.

question: Who are eligible to vote in Lok Sabha elections? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Citizens aged 18 and above who are not disqualified under the Constitution or any law
Citizens who have paid income tax
Only citizens with a government job
Only citizens aged 21 and above
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Citizens aged 18 and above who are not disqualified under the Constitution or any law

Explanation:
According to Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, every Indian citizen who is 18 years of age or older is entitled to vote in Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, unless disqualified under any law. The 61st Amendment (1988) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years. Payment of income tax or holding a government job is not a prerequisite for voting. Grounds for disqualification include bankruptcy, unsound mind, conviction for certain offenses, and corrupt practices. It is mandatory to have one's name in the electoral roll.

question: Which of the following is NOT a provision to disqualify the members of a political party on the ground of defection mentioned in the tenth schedule of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: If a member votes against his party will
If a party merges with another party
If a nominated member joins another party after 6 months of his seat
If an elected member joins another party after election
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is If a party merges with another party

Explanation:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', provides provisions for disqualifying members on grounds of defection. These include: a member voting against his party's whip, voluntarily giving up party membership, and an elected member joining another party after the election. Nominated members have a grace period of 6 months. However, if a party merges with another party, it is not considered defection, provided that at least two-thirds of the party's members agree to the merger. Hence, option 2 is NOT a provision for disqualification on the ground of defection.

question: The Right to Vote is: (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: a legal right
a Fundamental Right
a Fundamental Duty
neither a Fundamental Right nor a legal right
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a legal right

Explanation:
The Right to Vote in India is a legal and constitutional right, not a Fundamental Right. It is derived from Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, which provides for adult suffrage in elections to the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies. This right is exercised under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and other electoral laws. While Fundamental Rights like freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)) are enforceable by courts, the right to vote is subject to statutory provisions. The Supreme Court has affirmed that voting rights are governed by constitutional provisions and laws made by Parliament. Therefore, it is a legal right, not a Fundamental Right or Duty.

मतदान का अधिकार भारतीय संविधान के भाग 15 में निर्वाचन संबंधी प्रावधानों के तहत आता है। यह किसी नागरिक का संवैधानिक अधिकार है, लेकिन मौलिक अधिकार नहीं। भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 326 लोकसभा और विधानसभाओं के चुनावों में वयस्क मताधिकार का प्रावधान करता है। इस अधिकार को लागू करने के लिए संसद ने जनप्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 जैसे कानून बनाए हैं। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता जैसे मौलिक अधिकार हैं, लेकिन मतदान का अधिकार उनमें शामिल नहीं। यह एक वैधानिक (legal) और संवैधानिक अधिकार है। उच्चतम न्यायालय ने कहा है कि मतदान का अधिकार संवैधानिक प्रावधानों और संसद द्वारा बनाए गए कानूनों द्वारा शासित होता है।

question: Appeals from the judgments of a Family Court under the Family Courts Act, 1984, lie to which court? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: District Court
Family Court Tribunal
High Court
Supreme Court of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is High Court

Explanation:
Under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act, 1984, appeals from the judgments or orders of a Family Court lie to the High Court within whose jurisdiction the Family Court is situated. The appeal can be filed on grounds of error in fact or law. However, certain orders, such as interim orders or consent orders, are not appealable under Section 19(3). This provision aims to ensure speedy resolution of family disputes by limiting the appellate remedy to the High Court, thereby avoiding multiple layers of appeals. The High Court may also exercise its revisional powers in appropriate cases.

question_hi: 1984 के पारिवारिक न्यायालय अधिनियम के अंतर्गत पारिवारिक न्यायालय के निर्णयों से अपील किस न्यायालय में की जाती है? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: जिला न्यायालय
पारिवारिक न्यायालय ट्रिब्यूनल
उच्च न्यायालय
भारत का सर्वोच्च न्यायालय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उच्च न्यायालय

Explanation:
पारिवारिक न्यायालय अधिनियम, 1984 की धारा 19 के अनुसार, किसी पारिवारिक न्यायालय द्वारा पारित आदेश या निर्णय के विरुद्ध अपील संबंधित उच्च न्यायालय में की जा सकती है। यह अपील उस उच्च न्यायालय में दायर की जाती है जिसके अधिकार क्षेत्र में वह पारिवारिक न्यायालय स्थित है। अपील का कारण आदेश या निर्णय में तथ्य या विधि की त्रुटि हो सकती है। धारा 19(3) के तहत, कुछ मामलों में, जैसे अंतरिम आदेश या सहमति से पारित आदेश, अपील की अनुमति नहीं होती। यह प्रावधान पारिवारिक विवादों में त्वरित न्याय सुनिश्चित करने के लिए बनाया गया है।
